newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Niznhy Novgorod sees Eurobond issue in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Russia Niznhy Novgorod sees Eurobond issue in Sept.

text.p: Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region plans to issue its debut Eurobond in September after it has registered the issue prospectus with the Finance Ministry, a regional official said on Thursday.
"We shall make the issue in September, as soon as we register the prospectus with the Finance Ministry," securities issue department head Yuri Podlesov told Reuters.
He said the regional administration had passed the documents to the central bank to get a licence to repatriate hard currency revenues.

Nizhny Novogorod is one of the three Russian territories, which President Boris Yeltsin has authorised to issue Eurobonds. The other two, the City of Moscow and St Petersburg have already issued Eurobonds.
The forthcoming Nizhny Novgorod Eurobond, delayed because of recent gubernatorial elections, has been rated Ba2 by Moody's and BB- by Standard & Poor's.

Nizhny Novgorod is a major industrial centre on the River Volga about 300 km east of Moscow, with some of Russia's biggest automobile and engineering companies. Under its previous governor, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, it pioneered a series of radical economic reforms.
